candidates.why: At the call site (3129) decomp = sec_dat[type].chain, and dat can be the same Bit_Chain: dat is set to &sec_dat[sec_id] at 2936 and 3004. When type == sec_id, dat->chain and decomp alias the same buffer. Inside copy_R2004_section, bit_chain_alloc(dat) at 1422 does realloc(dat->chain) (bits.c:3015), which frees the old block; decomp still points to that freed block and is then read by memcpy at 1425 -> use-after-free (also a restrict violation).

sec_dat[type].chain is freed at 3113 and reassigned to decr at 3114. If calloc at 3108 returned NULL, sec_dat[type].chain becomes NULL and is passed as decomp to copy_R2004_section at 3129, where memcpy at 1425 dereferences it. Not a classic UAF but the freed pointer's slot is reused without a NULL check before the memcpy.

bit_chain_free(&sec_dat[type]) at 3133 frees sec_dat[type].chain and sets it NULL, but this is inside the k-loop over info->num_sections (3075). On the next iteration k+1, sec_dat[type].chain is NULL and the guard at 3083 only 'continue's, so no direct UAF; however sec->size (3129) is not re-validated against the buffer, so a stale/oversized sec->size can over-read decomp at 1425.
